$description: Promotion decisions for the motion contract's roles. tokens/contracts/motion.json records what a role IS and who consumes it; this file records whether anyone has decided that its `status` may read `proven`. The two are separate on purpose: the first is a description a branch may change as it adds a consumer, the second is an architecture decision that a branch must not take on its own. scripts/check-motion-promotion.mjs holds them to each other. This is not a token source and Style Dictionary does not read it.
$rule: motion.json's selection-indicator note states the rule this file enforces: a role is promoted to proven once a SECOND platform consumes it. So every role consumed by two or more platforms needs a decision here, and `proven` requires that decision to be `approved`. A role consumed by one platform needs no entry — there is nothing yet to decide.

$states.pending: The rule has been triggered and the decision is deliberately open. The role's status must stay `observed` (or `proposed`). `review` says what the decision is waiting on.
$states.approved: A promotion to `proven` is authorised. `approval.authority` says WHO authorised it, and `approval.basis` says on what — a reference a reviewer can check, not a restatement of the status.

approval.basis: Already `proven` on main before this register existed, with five platform consumers and five evidence files. Recorded here so the gate has the decision it requires; this entry documents a status that shipped, and is not a new authorisation.
Already `proven` on main before this register existed, with five platform consumers. Recorded, not newly authorised.
Already `proven` on main before this register existed, with five platform consumers and seven evidence files. Recorded, not newly authorised.
Already `proven` on main before this register existed, on two platform consumers — the rule's minimum. Recorded, not newly authorised.
Already `proven` on main before this register existed, with five platform consumers. Recorded, not newly authorised.

triggeredBy.note: Surfaced by this register rather than by a branch: `overlay` has had two platform consumers and `status: observed` with no recorded decision, so the rule was already triggered and nothing said so. No promotion is proposed here.

overlay.review: Open and previously unrecorded. Its single evidence file covers React only; Angular's side has no evidence entry. Decide whether to add Angular evidence and promote, or to state why `observed` is the right resting status for this role.

$note: selection-indicator has no entry: on main only React consumes it, so the rule is not triggered and there is nothing to decide. The branch that adds the second platform adds the decision — which is this register working, not a gap in it.
